transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Priya Nair, Liam O'Sullivan, Elena Rossi (Veridex)

Auto Summary: Quick renewal check-in focusing on committed capacity bump, EU region onboarding (data residency), and contract amendment timing. SE provided technical constraints for onprem/VPC path and suggested pilot benchmarks. Procurement requested pricing breakdown and legal contacts.

Topics: renewal capacity numbers, EU private onramp, KMS & audit logs, latency SLOs, canary/rollout approach, procurement timing, pilot benchmarks, competitor positioning.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about an hour on the calendar. Quick intros then we'll jump into the numbers and EU onramp path.
00:12 Priya (Veridex): Hi all, Priya here, we run the MLOps infra and I'll own the pilot. Liam on the call to give exec context, Elena for procurement.
00:20 Liam (Veridex): Hi, quick note — timeline is Q4 sign, Q1 EU go-live ideally.
00:30 Maya: Great, scope is renewal with a capacity uplift, and add EU hosting (data residency) — question for Diego: is Private or Dedicated the stronger fit?
00:45 Diego (Redwood): Short answer: it depends on the residency & isolation needs. If you need full VPC control + HSM/KMS in your cloud, Private with our private control plane is the path. Dedicated can meet isolation with reserved capacity but traffic may cross regions unless you pin geoclusters.
01:02 Priya: We need logs in-country and KMS integration to our Azure Key Vault; can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
01:15 Diego: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations, there may be a short security review. Note: we'll want a brief network design call to map VPC peering and routing for low egress latency.
01:30 Elena: From procurement — we'll need a clear statement on data residency and sample DPAs, and also the billing cadence (monthly vs annual). Also, do you support SSO/SAML?
01:45 Maya: Yes SSO/SAML + RBAC are available; we'll attach SOC2 docs and a standard DPA. I'll include that in the package.
02:00 Priya: On capacity, we're proposing a 2x committed token baseline with a burst tier; our usage has a strong tail — 95th percentile latency matters for product.
02:20 Diego: Understood. For 95th pctl latency at sub-300ms you'll want a combination of colocated EU geoclusters and KV cache warmers. We can do prefix caching for common prompts to reduce cold-token latency.
02:45 Liam: How do you handle fallbacks if EU capacity is saturated? We can't have user-facing outages.
03:00 Maya: We have a routing policy that will failover to the nearest compatible model/region, and you can configure graceful degradation — e.g., fall back to a smaller distilled model with a lower cost/latency profile. Diego, maybe outline the fallback options?
03:18 Diego: Right, automated fallback + canary rollouts. For strict residency constraints you can opt for strict-only routing (reject cross-region), but that carries outage risk. Most customers opt for allowed-fallback with logging and audit.
03:40 Priya: Okay, we prefer allowed-fallback logged with alerts. Also we need audit logs for all admin actions and token-level usage traces for cost allocation.
04:00 Maya: We can provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We'll include sample screenshots in the follow up.
04:18 Elena: Procurement will need a sample invoice and the PO flow. Do you do net-30?
04:30 Maya: Standard is net-30 for enterprise; we'll confirm in the SOW.
04:40 Priya: On the technical pilot — what's a realistic benchmarking sequence? We want end-to-end latencies, throughput at 90/95 percentiles, and hallucination/regression checks.
05:02 Diego: Pilot plan: 1) baseline synthetic load to emulate peak QPS, 2) token-level throughput and latency at varying sequence lengths, 3) cold vs warmed cache comparison, 4) example prompt set for quality/regression. We typically run a 2-week pilot to capture weekday/weekend patterns.
05:30 Liam: Two weeks is fine but we need results before procurement signs.
05:40 Maya: We'll aim to run pilot week of Sep 27 and have a readout within 5 business days.
05:52 Priya: What's the instrumentation — do you provide traces we can ingest into our observability stack?
06:05 Diego: Yes, tracing hooks and per-request IDs, you can forward traces to your preferred vendor; we also export logs to S3/buckets in region for retention.
06:20 Priya: Retention requirements — we may need 12 months for audit. Is that supported?
06:30 Maya: Yes, retention tiers are configurable; long-term retention is an add-on but supported.
06:42 Elena: On the contract amendment: is there flexibility around committed tokens being reallocated mid-term?
06:55 Maya: We can include an amendment clause for one-time reallocation per year, subject to pricing tiers. We'll propose terms.
07:10 Priya: Any gotchas in the EU onramp technically — e.g., difference between private onprem package vs private VPC?
07:25 Diego: Private VPC means your control plane still sits in our hosted control plane but traffic stays in your VPC via peering and your KMS. On-prem (air-gapped) is a heavier lift — you'll host the control plane and the runtime; that's typically reserved for regulated customers with strict sovereignty needs.
07:45 Priya: We're leaning VPC-first, not full on-prem. Latency budget is tight.
07:55 Diego: Good fit then. We'll size geocluster nodes to your peak and provide autoscaling and burst buffer. Note: quantization profiles (8-bit etc) can reduce memory and cost but sometimes affect quality; we'll provide model recommendations per workload.
08:18 Priya: Can you share previous benchmarks for similar customers in EU?
08:30 Diego: We can share anonymized benchmark snapshots — I'll include two case studies: retail chat workload and a financial Q&A workload.
08:45 Liam: Competitors — we tested LambdaCloud earlier, what are key diffs?
08:55 Maya: Main diffs are our unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, plus first-class observability and committed-capacity pricing that tends to be more predictable. Also we do more workload-aware batching and KV cache to keep unit costs down.
09:12 Elena: Legal will want breach notification SLAs and subprocessor lists.
09:20 Maya: We'll include breach notification timelines and SSO/SAML details, plus subprocessors in the security packet.
09:32 Priya: For the pilot we'll need a small dedicated pool — how many GPUs should we expect to reserve for realistic throughput test?
09:45 Diego: Based on your traffic profile (you'll send it after the call) I'd recommend starting with 2x A100-equivalent instances for the pilot and scale from there. We'll provide cost estimates.
10:05 Priya: Our peak is roughly 120 requests/minute with average sequence length 350 tokens. Does that map to your 2x estimate?
10:20 Diego: Yes that's in the ballpark; we'll run a calculator and share token/sec numbers in the follow-up.
10:32 Maya: Let me recap before we open for questions: 1) we'll send pricing + DPA + SOC2 + sample SOW; 2) Diego shares VPC/KMS runbook + benchmark checklist; 3) Veridex shares traffic profile and internal sign-off timeline; 4) schedule pilot week of Sep 27.
10:55 Priya: Sounds good. Quick question on billing: if we commit annually but want to add mid-term EU region, how is that priced?
11:08 Maya: We typically prorate the additional reserved capacity and amortize across remaining months, but we can propose a simplified amendment that locks the new committed rate for the remaining term.
11:22 Elena: We'll need the exact amendment language for legal review.
11:33 Diego: One more technical note — if you enable strict residency, fallback to other regions will be disabled; recommend allowed-fallback with audit for user experience.
11:48 Priya: Agreed.
11:52 Liam: Procurement note — can you provide an estimated TCO delta for enabling EU region vs hosting cross-region? We want to present both to board.
12:05 Maya: We'll run a comparative TCO with assumptions and include it in the follow-up.
12:18 Priya: Any regulatory concerns around PII and model outputs? We want to ensure we can redact PHI/PPI before logs land in storage.
12:32 Diego: Redaction hooks are supported; you can mask tokens pre-ingest and we can configure log redaction. We'll document the hook points.
12:45 Elena: Final timeline ask — legal sign-off target is Oct 8 to make Q4 prep. Can Redwood meet that?
12:58 Maya: Yes, if we deliver docs by Sep 13 and pilot wraps early Oct, that's feasible.
13:10 Priya: Anything else on your side?
13:15 Maya: That's it. We'll follow up with the package. Thanks everyone.
13:22 Liam: Thanks.

Recap (auto-generated): Agreed items: committed capacity uplift proposed (2x baseline), EU VPC-onramp chosen (not on-prem), pilot week of Sep 27, deliverables due by Sep 13 & Sep 17, procurement timeline aiming for Oct 8 sign-off.

References/shared links mentioned in call: Pricing spreadsheet (link to be attached), Security packet (SOC2/DPA), VPC runbook & benchmark checklist (to be attached).

End transcript.
